question: How many copies of the same named card can I put in my Main Deck?
answer: Your Main Deck can include up to 3 copies of the same named card [rule 103.3.b]. This limit includes your Chosen Champion [rule 103.3.b.1].

question: How many runes are in a Rune Deck?
answer: Exactly 12 Rune cards are chosen during Deck Construction for the Rune Deck [rule 161.2.a].

question: During the mulligan, what is the maximum number of cards I can set aside?
answer: A player may choose up to two cards in their hand during the Mulligan [rule 117.1]. They then draw as many cards as they set aside [rule 117.2].

question: What happens to the cards I set aside during my mulligan?
answer: The cards you set aside during your mulligan are Recycled [rule 117.3]. You may choose up to two cards in your hand to set aside [rule 117.1]. Then, you draw as many cards as you set aside [rule 117.2].

question: How many points do you need to win by default?
answer: The Victory Score is 8 points by default [rule 194.3]. A player wins the game if, in a cleanup, they have points greater than or equal to the Victory Score and more points than any other player [rule 194.2].

question: What is the Victory Score in 2v2 Magma Chamber?
answer: The Victory Score in 2v2 (Magma Chamber) is 11 [rule 491.3]. This format is played as a Best of 1 match [rule 491.6].

question: Can a player's point total go below zero?

question: How many runes does the turn player channel in the Channel Phase?
answer: The Turn Player channels 2 runes from their Rune Deck during the Channel Phase [rule 315.3.b.1]. If there are fewer than 2 runes in the Rune Deck, they channel as many as possible [rule 315.3.b.1].

question: What happens if I need to draw a card but my Main Deck is empty?
answer: If a player must draw cards in excess to the number of cards in their Main Deck, they will draw as many as possible, perform the Burn Out action, and then draw the remaining amount instructed [rule 432.1.a]. To Burn Out, a player recycles their trash into their Main Deck, randomizing it, and then chooses an opponent to gain 1 point [rule 432.2.b, 432.2.c].

question: In a 1v1 Duel, what bonus does the player going second get?
answer: The player going second channels an extra Rune from their Rune Deck during their first Channel Phase of the game [rule 487.7]. The Victory Score for a 1v1 Duel is 8 [rule 487.3].

question: How many battlefields does each player bring to a 1v1 Duel?
answer: Each player provides three (3) Battlefields, which are included in their deck during deck building [rule 487.4.a]. Only one of these Battlefields is used during setup [rule 487.5].

question: How many games are in a 1v1 Match?
answer: A 1v1 Match is a Best of 3 format [rule 488.6]. The first player to reach the Victory Score in Points wins the game [rule 488.6]. The first player to earn Two Game Wins wins the match [rule 488.6].

question: When is a unit considered Mighty?
answer: A Unit "is Mighty" as long as its Might is 5 or greater [rule 708]. Units in Non-Board Zones are evaluated according to their printed Might [rule 711].

question: How much Might does a single buff give a unit?
answer: Each Buff individually contributes +1 Might to a Unit [rule 703].

question: Can a unit have more than one buff at a time?
answer: There can only be one Buff on a Unit at a time [rule 702.3]. If a Buff is added to a Unit that already has a Buff, it is not placed instead [rule 702.3.a]. However, some effects may grant a Game Object permission to be Buffed multiple times, which ignores this restriction [rule 427.1.b.2].

question: What does the Shield keyword do?
answer: Shield is a Passive Ability keyword present on Units [rule 814.1.a]. It is formatted as "Shield [X]" [rule 814.1.b]. If a Unit has Shield, or has been granted Shield, and is granted Shield by an additional source, the Shield Value of all granted Shield keywords is summed [rule 814.2].

question: What does the Tank keyword do?
answer: Tank is a Passive Ability keyword present on Units [rule 815.1.a]. It functionally means the unit must be assigned lethal damage before any other unit with the same controller that does not have Tank during the Combat Damage step [rule 815.1.b.1]. This alters how players can elect to assign combat damage during combat [rule 815.1.c].

question: What does Ganking let a unit do?
answer: Ganking is a passive ability that adds permissions to a Unit's Standard Move [rule 810.1.c]. Specifically, Units with Ganking may use their Standard Move to Move from Battlefield to Battlefield [rule 144.4.c.1]. It is functionally short for "I may move to a battlefield from another battlefield with a standard move" [rule 810.1.b].

question: What happens if I pay the Accelerate cost when playing a unit?
answer: If you pay the Accelerate cost, the unit will enter ready [805.2.b]. This generates a Delayed Replacement Effect, meaning the unit enters ready even if it loses the Accelerate keyword during finalization [805.2.b, 805.6].

question: What does Deathknell mean?
answer: Deathknell is a Triggered Ability keyword present on Permanents [rule 808.1.a]. It is functionally short for "When I die, [Effect]" [rule 808.1.c]. The trigger occurs when the Permanent is Killed and sent to the Trash [rule 808.1.d].

question: When is a player allowed to concede?
answer: A player may concede at any time [rule 650]. When a player concedes, they are removed from the game in progress [rule 651].

question: Is there a maximum amount of XP a player can have?
answer: There is no limit to an amount of XP a player can accrue [rule 733]. XP is a resource that can be accrued, spent, or otherwise modified by Players [rule 729].

question: Does a stunned unit deal combat damage?
answer: A Stunned Unit does not contribute its might to damage in the combat damage step [rule 424.1.b].

question: What two kinds of resources do runes produce?
answer: Runes produce Energy and Power [rule 163]. Energy is used to pay numeric Energy costs [rule 163.1], and Power is used to pay Domain-associated Power Costs [rule 163.2].

question: What happens to damage on units at the end of the turn?
answer: Damage on Units is Healed at the end of each player's turn [rule 143.3.b.1].

question: How many times can I score the same battlefield in one turn?
answer: A player may only Score, from either method, once per Battlefield per turn [rule 472].

question: I conquer a battlefield when I'm one point from winning, but I haven't scored every battlefield this turn. What happens?
answer: If you try to Gain a Point through a Conquer when your current Point Total is 1 point from the Victory Score of the Mode of Play or higher, and you have not Scored every Battlefield this turn, you draw a card instead [rule 473.1.b.1].

question: In 3-player Skirmish, what is different about the first player's first turn?
must_include: not draw|doesn't draw|does not draw|no card|skip|skips
answer: In 3-player Skirmish, the player going first does not draw a card during their first Draw Phase of the game [rule 489.7]. The player going last channels an extra Rune from their Rune Deck during their first Channel Phase of the game [rule 489.7].
